title: Compact usage shard mart for real-time console queries
creator: Alicia Mendez
description: Design and implement a compact denormalized usage shard mart to serve low-latency console queries (SLO dashboards, per-route SLA slices, and tenant quick lookups). The goal is sub-second single-tenant queries for common access patterns while keeping storage growth bounded and making backfills tractable. This ticket covers schema design, partitioning/clustering strategy, ingestion transforms, incremental mview wiring, and a migration plan from existing wide-session tables.
acceptance_criteria: Create compact shard mart schema that supports: per-tenant daily/hourly aggregates, recent N-day rolling windows, and fast point lookups by route+tenant+day
Demonstrate 95th percentile query latency < 800ms for typical console queries on staged dataset (scale model: 50k tenants, hot 5%)
End-to-end ETL that populates shard mart in near-real-time (<5min freshness) for hot tenants via streaming micro-batches
Storage growth estimate and cost projection document produced and approved (<25% additional storage vs current denorm strategy for same retention),
Backfill tooling that can fill historical range without blowing up cluster (throttled, idempotent, resumable).
migration_plan: Phase 0: Spike and validation on 7-day sampled tenant set; run both existing and shard mart queries side-by-side
Phase 1: Publish schema and ingest pipeline to staging; enable mview with materialized snapshots and incremental deltas
Phase 2: Canary with 2% of tenants flagged as hot; validate latencies and cost metrics; run smoke dashboards
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with monitoring alerts and automatic fallback to denorm tables on error
Rollback: Swap query routing to legacy views and disable mviews; backfill jobs are idempotent so restart safe
decisions: Use daily partitioning with hourly sub-partitions (partition_key = date, cluster_key = tenant_id) to balance partition pruning and compaction
Store numeric aggregates and small enumerated tags; avoid storing wide JSON payloads in shard mart (keep references to canonical event store)
Use columnar storage (Parquet/ORC on our lake) for long-term retention and row-oriented materialized snapshots for the hot mart layer
Implement TTL of 90 days in hot mart with automated cold-archive into long-term parquet snapshot buckets
